STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a large dinner-size square plate, roughly 25-27 cm.
b) Reference: the kale salad mound spans roughly 40% of the plate's width, and the plate's visible width is about 2.5-3 times the mound's spread. A typical kale mound would be ~10-11 cm across, which puts the plate near 26 cm.
Reconciled width: 26 cm (area 676 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Kale salad (cooked-looking/massaged raw kale with dressing): the mound covers about 22% of the plate, roughly 149 cm2. Mound averages about half its peak; peak ~3 cm of loose leaves, so average ~1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 149 × 1.5 = 224 ml. Raw massaged kale with dressing, bulk density ~0.3 g/ml (leafy greens mixed with dressing, lightly packed). Grams ≈ 224 × 0.3 ≈ 67 g.
- Parmesan/hard cheese shavings and chunks: two visible pieces (~2 cm and ~1.5 cm), plus shavings scattered through the salad. Estimate ~8 g of cheese.
- Dressing (oil-based, visible sheen, coating the leaves): estimate ~6 g.
- Nut/crumb pieces (small, one visible at the right edge): ~2 g.

Total ≈ 67 + 8 + 6 + 2 ≈ 83 g.

Energy (kcal per 100 g):
- Kale salad with dressing base (mostly kale, some oil): ~60 kcal/100 g (kale ~35, dressing lifts it).
- Hard cheese (Parmesan): ~390 kcal/100 g.
- Dressing/oil: ~550 kcal/100 g... listed per item as served, so I use the dressing value as the salad component split out separately below.
- Nut/crumb: ~550 kcal/100 g.

To keep items distinct: kale base 67 g at 60 kcal/100 g = 40 kcal; cheese 8 g at 390 = 31 kcal; dressing 6 g at 550 = 33 kcal; nut 2 g at 550 = 11 kcal. Total ≈ 115 kcal for ~83 g.
